items.text: REMINDER

items.label: text
items.text: If you have forgotten about oxidation and reduction, you might find it useful to re-read Chapter 14.

items.label: section_header
items.text: METALS BELOW CARBON IN THE REACTIVITY SERIES

items.label: text
items.text: To obtain the metal from the oxide, you have to remove the oxygen. Removal of oxygen is called reduction. Metals exist as positive ions in their ionic compounds, and to produce the metal you would have to add electrons to the positive ion. Addition of electrons is also called reduction.

items.label: section_header
items.text: METHODS OF EXTRACTION AND THE REACTIVITY SERIES

items.label: text
items.text: How a metal is extracted depends to a large extent on its position in the reactivity series. A manufacturer obviously wants to use the cheapest possible method of extracting a metal from an ore. There are two main economic factors to take into account:

items.label: list_item
items.text: the cost of energy

items.label: list_item
items.text: the cost of the reducing agent.

items.label: text
items.text: For a metal below carbon in the reactivity series, the cheapest method of reducing the ore is often to heat it with carbon.

items.label: text
items.text: The extraction of iron is a good example of this. One of the main ores of iron contains a high percentage of iron(Ill) oxide. The iron can be extracted from this by heating with carbon:

items.label: formula
items.text: F e _ { 2 } O _ { 3 } ( s ) + 3 C ( s ) \rightarrow 2 F e ( 1 ) + 3 C O ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: Carbon is higher in the reactivity series than iron and will take the oxygen away from the iron oxide. This is a redox reaction; the Fe2O₃is reduced to Fe in the reaction and the C is oxidised to CO. In this reaction the carbon is the reducing agent, it reduces the iron(III) oxide.
